applied_items.content:
Canonical checkpoint. The helper SHALL keep one canonical checkpoint per open session: the front matter of the active session's `session.md` (REQ-records-004, REQ-cli-037), holding the objective, intent scope, modules, current stage with its status, iteration and side-stage callers, the native change identity, the pull request, referenced criteria, requirements, cases, design sources and files, observation and bug references, blockers, awaiting-human gates, run consents and the next action, with decisions, completed work and open questions in the story sections of the same file. No other writable checkpoint store SHALL exist and no adapter such as APS SHALL be required. Every read SHALL validate the front matter's keys and value types and SHALL refuse a malformed one naming the file, the key and the rule (REQ-records-001). `chough checkpoint --merge` and the `chough-session` merge driver are removed, because each session has its own folder and parallel branches never write one checkpoint (DRIVE-24). When SpecSync is configured, `chough checkpoint --native-change <id>` SHALL read `specsync change status <id>` before it applies any update, and SHALL refuse as `refused:native-change-unknown`, naming the ID and that status command, when SpecSync does not report the change; a failed or timed-out read SHALL also refuse, and a reply whose `summary.id` or `change.id` names a different change SHALL refuse as `refused:native-change-mismatch`, naming both IDs. A JSON reply that names neither `summary.id` nor `change.id` SHALL refuse as `refused:native-change-unknown`, since it does not identify the requested change. Every such refusal SHALL leave the session file byte-identical, including the other updates given in the same call. An ID SpecSync reports, archived or open, SHALL be saved as before. Without a SpecSync configuration only the existing ID format check SHALL apply, with no native read. Trace: FLOW-13, LIFE-3, DRIVE-3, DRIVE-24, DRIVE-25.

Acceptance Criteria
- A checkpoint saved by one process is read unchanged by `chough context` and `chough next` in another process; a front matter key with the wrong type is refused naming the file and the key, with nothing written.
- No second writable checkpoint store is introduced and no adapter is required; `.gitattributes` declares no `chough-session` driver and `chough checkpoint --merge` is not a command.
- With SpecSync configured, `checkpoint --native-change` for an ID SpecSync does not report, or after a failed or timed-out status read, exits non-zero with `refused:native-change-unknown` or the read failure and leaves the session file byte-identical even with other updates in the same call; a reply naming a different change refuses as `refused:native-change-mismatch` with the file byte-identical; a JSON reply naming no change ID, such as `[]` or `{}`, refuses as `refused:native-change-unknown` with the file byte-identical; a reported ID saves; without SpecSync any well-formed ID saves and a malformed one is refused.

Canonical checkpoint and explicit migration. The helper SHALL keep one canonical checkpoint at `.chough/session.json` or, in sessions mode, the active session file (REQ-cli-037), schema version 2, holding the objective, intent scope, modules, current stage with its status and side-stage callers, the native change identity, referenced criteria, requirements, cases, design sources and files, decisions, open questions, completed work, observation and bug references, blockers, awaiting-human gates, run consents and the next action. It SHALL migrate a schema 1 session only through an explicit command that first preserves the original bytes, and SHALL keep reading schema 1 sessions for context and status. Trace: FLOW-13, LIFE-3, DRIVE-3.

The helper SHALL provide bounded `chough checkpoint --merge <base> <ours> <theirs>` for three-way reconciliation of schema 2 checkpoints. For `decisions`, `open_questions`, `completed`, `observations`, `bugs` and every collection under `references`, entries SHALL be compared as exact strings. Base entries not removed on either side SHALL retain base order, entries added by ours SHALL follow in ours order with an identical addition on both sides included once, and remaining entries added by theirs SHALL follow in theirs order. An entry removed on only one side SHALL remain removed.

The complete values of `objective`, `intent_scope`, `modules`, `stage`, `native_change`, `next_action`, `run_consents`, `blockers` and `awaiting_human` SHALL form one current-cycle group. If neither side changes that group from base, the merge SHALL select base; if exactly one side changes it, the merge SHALL select that side's complete group; if both sides make the identical change, the merge SHALL select that group. If both sides change it differently, the merge SHALL refuse with a current-cycle conflict reason rather than combine fields or select a side.

Every input SHALL be read within the existing checkpoint bounds and validated without unknown fields. All three inputs SHALL use schema version 2, and the merged result SHALL satisfy every existing checkpoint bound before it is written. A successful merge SHALL write the result only to `<ours>`, leaving `<base>` and `<theirs>` byte-identical. Every refusal SHALL leave all three inputs byte-identical and SHALL create no checkpoint, transition, gate, consent, approval, review or other record. This reconciliation path SHALL NOT change one-owner live writes, native SpecSync authority or any non-checkpoint ID scheme, and SHALL NOT introduce a second writable checkpoint store.

The repository SHALL declare `.chough/session.json merge=chough-session` in `.gitattributes`, and the same driver for `.chough/sessions/*.json` and `.chough/sessions/archive/*.json`. Documentation SHALL give the per-clone command `git config merge.chough-session.driver 'chough checkpoint --merge %O %A %B'`; initialization SHALL NOT change Git configuration. The explicit merge command SHALL remain the fallback when no driver is configured.

Identical repeated runs SHALL stay distinct history: same-day runs of one case in one session get clash suffixes. Creation SHALL use atomic create-new; a same-name different-content creation SHALL be refused without overwriting the existing bytes and without a numeric, timestamp or digest fallback, another random draw or any other retry. Serialized record writers. Every command that writes a Chough record SHALL hold one writer lock for the project while it reads what it changes and saves it, so a concurrent writer applies its change to the latest records and no update is lost. The lock SHALL be the file `.chough/local/checkpoint.lock` inside the project, in a directory Git ignores, so every process working on the project uses the same lock whatever its temporary directory. A writer that cannot take the lock within 30 seconds SHALL refuse as `refused:checkpoint-busy`, naming the record it would write, with nothing saved. On taking the lock a writer SHALL record its process ID in the lock file, and a `refused:checkpoint-busy` refusal SHALL name the process ID the file holds, if any, so a lock held by a forked child's inherited descriptor (#132) can be told from a live writer. Read-only commands SHALL take no lock. Trace: DRIVE-11, DRIVE-3.

- Linking a bug to itself or to an unknown bug, as duplicate or related, and updating or reporting an unknown bug, are refused with nothing written and name `chough bug list --all`, which lists the bugs.

Append-only timeline. Each session's transitions SHALL be recorded as entries of the `## Timeline` section of its `session.md` (REQ-records-004), and those entries, carried into the archived story at finish, SHALL be the session's only transition history: no event file, cycle directory, cursor or transitions log SHALL be written. Each entry SHALL be one list item, `- <time> · <kind> · <from> → <to> · <text> ^<entry id>`, where `<time>` is the UTC time to the second in ISO 8601, `<kind>` is a transition kind (`advance`, `iterate`, `back`, `reset`, `pause`, `resume`, `skip`, `enter`, `return`, `gate-opened`, `gate-closed`, `direct-native-write`, `correction`), `<text>` is the reason, gate or note, and `<entry id>` is `t-` and 6 lowercase hexadecimal digits from fresh random bits, unique in the file. Its structured fields SHALL follow as indented `- <key>: <value>` lines: `by` for the actor (REQ-records-007), `native_change` when one is recorded, and the fields of REQ-history-005, REQ-history-010, REQ-history-013, REQ-history-014 and REQ-history-015. The entry and the checkpoint change it goes with SHALL be written in the same atomic replace of `session.md`, so a refused or failed save leaves neither. Chough SHALL only append entries: it SHALL never edit, reorder or remove an existing entry line, and an entry ID SHALL never be reused in its file. A timeline entry is what other requirements call a transition, and the session file's Timeline is what they call its transition log. `chough doctor` SHALL report a session or story whose Timeline at HEAD is not an exact prefix of its Timeline in the working tree (REQ-history-012). applied_items.content: Retired in Chough 0.6.0: committed observation sets no longer pile up for retention to prune. Evidence lives in its session and folds into the archived story at finish (REQ-history-006), raw logs are never committed (REQ-records-005), and files leave the tree only under REQ-records-012. `chough evidence prune` and the retention ledger are removed; LIFE-8's removed-not-passed rule is kept by REQ-records-009.
applied_items.previous_content:
Reference-aware retention. The helper SHALL preview by default which observation sets (a record and the artifacts only it references) are eligible for removal and which are protected and why, and SHALL protect sets referenced by the checkpoint, a bug, an active or the most recent archived native change, non-routine records, the newest runs and newest failure per case and environment, validation failures and boundary passes, and recent sets. It SHALL remove eligible sets only under a run consent or a standing retention preference set by a human, SHALL record each removal in an append-only ledger, and SHALL label referenced observations current, historical, pruned or unavailable, never treating pruned or unavailable ones as current or passed. It SHALL NOT change native archives, ignore rules or Git history. Trace: LIFE-8, LIFE-2, LIFE-7, FLOW-7, FLOW-13.

Acceptance Criteria
- The preview changes no file and lists eligible and protected sets with reasons and reclaimed bytes.
- Apply without consent or the standing preference is refused.
- A pruned observation referenced anywhere is reported pruned, and a missing unlisted one unavailable; neither is current or passed.

applied_items.content: Retired in Chough 0.6.0 with `chough evidence prune` and the retention ledger (see REQ-history-001); REQ-records-012 keeps the rule that only committed bytes ever leave the tree.
applied_items.previous_content:
Conservative evidence cleanup. Evidence retention SHALL keep the existing eligibility thresholds, protection semantics and ledger entry shape, rebuild protection at apply and revalidate candidate identity and safe paths immediately before removal. Changed, missing, shared, newly referenced or unsafe files SHALL be retained or refused with explicit outcomes. Immediately before every artifact and observation removal, apply SHALL recheck the protection fingerprint and SHALL remove through a byte-checked hold rather than a direct unlink. After a set's ledger line, a later check or removal failure SHALL restore every earlier removal with create-new writes and original permissions, without replacing a file recreated meanwhile. Original bytes that cannot be restored SHALL be retained under `.chough/removing/` and named in the refusal; apply SHALL NOT assume Git HEAD contains them. A `restored` event with the existing ledger shape SHALL be appended for each ledgered set, and the failed apply SHALL NOT be reported as completed pruning. Interrupted cleanup SHALL distinguish present content, recorded removal and unavailable history. It SHALL preserve the active checkpoint, migration backup, historical retained proof, native archives and every artifact still referenced by another observation. Trace: LIFE-2, LIFE-7, LIFE-8, FLOW-7, FLOW-13.

Acceptance Criteria
- Adding a checkpoint, bug, case or native protection reference after preview protects the relevant observation/cycle when apply runs.
- Shared artifacts remain present and byte-identical; missing/changed candidates, malformed sources, path traversal and symlinks cannot broaden deletion or be reported as a successful complete cleanup.
- Fault injection around publication/removal yields an actionable partial outcome and leaves active state and protected bytes intact. No existing observation, artifact fingerprint or evidence-ledger schema is rewritten.
- A protection appearing between two removals stops the apply and restores every earlier removal byte-for-byte with original permissions, including every completely removed earlier set; a later artifact or observation removal failure does the same and appends the existing `restored` event for each ledgered set.
- A file recreated during rollback is kept as written, the original uncommitted bytes are preserved in a named create-only hold under `.chough/removing/`, the refusal names every unrestored path and hold, and successful apply output and existing eligibility, authorization, bounds and ledger behavior remain unchanged.

applied_items.content: Retired in Chough 0.6.0: there are no separate event files to orphan. A timeline entry and its checkpoint change are one atomic replace of `session.md` (REQ-history-002), and `session use` and `session new` still wait for a running writer (REQ-cli-040, REQ-history-009).
applied_items.previous_content:
No orphan event from a vanished checkpoint. When a command's save is refused because the checkpoint it resolved was archived, removed or adopted into sessions mode while it ran, the helper SHALL first remove the history events that command published, and any cycle directory it reserved that is then empty, when their bytes are unchanged and they were published after the command last found its checkpoint in place. A save finds its checkpoint in place just before it writes, so the helper leaves no orphan event and never removes an event a save may have written, wherever that checkpoint is moved afterwards. Any other failed save SHALL keep REQ-history-002's unselected orphan. Chough's own `session use` and `session new` SHALL wait for a running checkpoint writer rather than archive or switch its session under it. Trace: DRIVE-3, LIFE-7.

Acceptance Criteria
- A `stage advance` whose session file is moved away during its native read refuses with nothing saved and leaves no new event file.
- `session use` started during a `stage advance` waits for it, and the advance records exactly its own event.
- A session file moved away after a successful save keeps the event that save points to.
- A session file moved after a successful save to a path outside `.chough/sessions/` keeps the event that save points to.

applied_items.content: Retired in Chough 0.6.0 and superseded by KNOW-30 and KNOW-34: archived session stories are never moved, copied or trimmed into the vault, and every one stays in `.chough/archive/sessions/` (REQ-history-006, REQ-records-012). The roll-up caused the data loss of issue 165, whose regression REQ-history-006 carries.
applied_items.previous_content:
Archived session roll-up. When `chough stage advance` moves into done and its save succeeds, with the librarian on, after the trim of REQ-cli-041 and before the knowledge refresh of REQ-cli-043, the helper SHALL keep in `.chough/sessions/archive/` only the five most recent archived sessions, apart from the session that adopted the legacy history. Recency SHALL be the finalization timestamp of the session's native change, newest first, then the key, the later key first. A session without a native change, or whose change has no readable finalization, SHALL count as the oldest. The archived session whose history cursor holds the legacy anchor (the session that adopted the legacy history) SHALL never be rolled into the vault: it SHALL stay in `.chough/sessions/archive/` in addition to the five and SHALL NOT count toward them, so history never depends on the knowledge directory. Each other archived session SHALL move byte for byte to `<library-dir>/attachments/<folder of its key>/sessions/<key>.json`, with the folder formed as in REQ-cli-046, and SHALL never replace a file. An attachment that already holds the same bytes SHALL be kept, and the source removed. One that holds different bytes SHALL leave the session in place and be reported. It SHALL report `applied.session_rollup` with status `rolled` and the moved keys, `unchanged`, `skipped` (librarian off), or `refused` with its reason, and SHALL NOT undo the move into done. A rolled session is no longer a retention reference source: its cycle is closed, and its native archive keeps what the change touched. `session list` SHALL NOT list it. Nothing SHALL be deleted from Git history. Trace: KNOW-29, DRIVE-13, KNOW-13.

Acceptance Criteria
- With seven archived sessions, five tied to archives finalized 60 to 20 days ago, one tied with the oldest, and one without a native change, the move into done keeps the five newest in `.chough/sessions/archive/` and moves the other two byte for byte into `knowledge/attachments/<key>/sessions/<key>.json`, reported as `rolled`.
- With the librarian off, no session moves and the step reports `skipped`.
- With seven archived sessions of which only the one that would roll first holds the legacy anchor, the move into done keeps that session and the five newest of the other six in `.chough/sessions/archive/`, rolls only the remaining one, and the anchor holder has no copy in the vault.

applied_items.content:
Timing report. The helper SHALL provide a read-only timing report derived from existing records: stage segments from transitions, including iterations, back, reset, skip, pause and resume, and side-stage enter and return; case observations and repeated-run summaries; bug creation, reproduction and verification; and the native lifecycle times native SpecSync exposes. It SHALL append a timestamped transition when an awaiting-human gate opens and one when it is cleared, and SHALL report active time separately from paused time and from time waiting on a human, without recording who decided or what. Every duration SHALL be labelled elapsed wall-clock time, not effort; history summaries SHALL give ranges with their sample count, labelled estimates rather than targets; a missing, unparseable or out-of-order timestamp SHALL be reported unknown, never zero. Transitions SHALL be read from each session's timeline, in open sessions and archived stories alike (REQ-history-002), and case observations, with their run times from `duration_seconds` when known, from evidence entries and the receipts of archived stories and bugs (REQ-cli-017), within the bounds of REQ-history-003; a session or story that cannot be read SHALL be named and the report marked partial. Inputs SHALL be bounded, and the report SHALL write no record. Trace: LIFE-10, DRIVE-24, LIFE-3, LIFE-6, LIFE-7.

Acceptance Criteria
- Fixture transitions with fixed timestamps for every transition kind yield the expected segments, gate records and `direct-native-write` events (REQ-history-013) start or end no segment, a `direct-native-write` event is not counted as an unrecognised kind, and paused and waiting-on-human time are excluded from active time.
- Opening a gate appends one gate-opened transition and clearing it one gate-closed transition; the report shows its waiting time, and a gate-opened record whose gate is no longer awaiting a human, with no gate-closed record, is reported closed at an unknown time.
- A missing timestamp or an end before its start is reported unknown, not zero, and fewer than three samples are reported too few to estimate.
- Running the report leaves every Chough and SpecSync record byte-identical, and input beyond its bound is reported partial.
- With one open session and three archived stories, the report gives each session's stage segments and gate waits from its timeline and each case's runs from entries and receipts; an unreadable story is named and the report is marked partial.
- No file under `.chough/history/` or `.chough/transitions.jsonl` is read.

applied_items.content:
Record files. Every record Chough writes, a session, an archived session story, an evidence entry, a bug, an inbox entry, a journal post and a migration receipt, SHALL be one UTF-8 Markdown file that starts with YAML front matter between two `---` lines, and that file SHALL be the record's only source of truth: no JSON or other twin SHALL be written beside it, and no index, cache or generated note SHALL be read in its place. The front matter SHALL carry the IDs and fields agents parse; the body SHALL carry the record for a human reader. Front matter SHALL use a strict subset of YAML that Chough reads and writes without a new dependency: `key: value` scalars, plain or double-quoted with `\"`, `\\` and `\n` escapes; flow lists `[a, b]`; block lists of scalars; and block lists of flat maps of scalars. Chough SHALL refuse front matter outside that subset, a duplicate key or a missing closing `---`, naming the file, the line and the rule, and SHALL write nothing in that command. Reading SHALL be tolerant: an unknown front matter key SHALL be kept byte for byte, in place, when Chough rewrites the front matter, and SHALL be ignored otherwise; a missing optional key SHALL take its documented default; CRLF line endings SHALL be read as LF. Chough SHALL own only the front matter and the sections it appends to, and SHALL keep every other body byte a person or agent wrote: a write SHALL replace the front matter, append list items to the end of a named section, or create a missing named section at the end of the body, and SHALL do nothing else to an existing body. Files SHALL be written with LF line endings by an atomic replace under the writer lock of REQ-cli-040, or by create-new for a new record. A record SHALL be at most 65,536 bytes, except a session record, an archived session story and a migration receipt, which SHALL be at most 1,048,576, 1,048,576 and 4,194,304 bytes; a record over its bound SHALL be refused with the bound named and every file byte-identical. Trace: DRIVE-25, DRIVE-26, DRIVE-28, KNOW-32, LIFE-3.

Acceptance Criteria
- Every record kind written by a fixture cycle (session, archived story, evidence, bug, inbox entry, journal post, migration receipt) starts with front matter that the reader parses, and no `.json` file is written under `.chough/` except the local caches of REQ-history-007 and `.chough/preferences.json`.
- A person's edit to a session's Goal paragraph, to a bug's Steps and to an evidence entry's body survives a following stage move, decision, evidence add and bug update byte for byte.
- An unknown front matter key added by hand is kept byte for byte after Chough rewrites that front matter, and a missing optional key reads as its default.
- Front matter with a nested map, an anchor, a duplicate key or no closing line is refused with the file, line and rule named, and nothing is written.
- A CRLF copy of a record reads the same as the LF original.
- A record one byte over its bound is refused naming the bound, with every file unchanged.

The records tree and its reading guides. Chough's committed records SHALL live in this tree: `.chough/README.md`; `.chough/sessions/<id>/session.md` with its `evidence/` and `agent/` folders, for open sessions; `.chough/archive/sessions/<id>.md`, one file per finished session, with `.chough/archive/sessions/<id>/` beside it only for its key screenshots (REQ-records-013); `.chough/archive/shelved/<id>/`, for shelved sessions; `.chough/archive/migrations/<id>.md`, for migration receipts; `.chough/bugs/<id>.md`; `.chough/cases/*.cases.toml`, case definitions in their existing TOML format (REQ-cli-009, REQ-cli-047); `.chough/preferences.json` (REQ-cli-013); and, kept from 0.5.x, the files under `.chough/artifacts/` that an open bug names as its fixture (REQ-records-009). Machine-local facts SHALL live only in the Git-ignored `.chough/local/` (REQ-history-007). Each kind of file SHALL have a stated rule: a session folder lives while its work is open and leaves the tree once its story is written and its bytes are committed; an archived story stays for good; a bug file stays for good; case definitions and preferences are configuration a person edits; and machine-only files live in `.chough/local/` and are never committed. `chough init` and `chough migrate --apply` SHALL write `.chough/README.md` create-only, a one-screen guide in plain words that names each folder, what it holds and its rule, which folder is never committed, and that intent lives in `hi/`, contracts in `specs/` and change history in `.specsync/archive/`, each a link, with no copy of their content; an existing `.chough/README.md` SHALL be kept byte-identical. `knowledge/index.md` is the vault's reading guide (REQ-cli-043). Chough SHALL write no other committed file or folder under `.chough/`, and SHALL NOT read a 0.5.x path except in `chough migrate` and `chough doctor` (REQ-records-010). Trace: DRIVE-24, DRIVE-28, KNOW-32, KNOW-24.

Acceptance Criteria
- After `chough init` in a new project, `.chough/` holds `README.md`, `cases/` and `local/` (ignored by Git), and `.chough/README.md` names every folder of the tree, says that `local/` is never committed, and links `hi/`, `specs/` and `.specsync/archive/`.
- `chough init` and `chough migrate --apply` over an existing `.chough/README.md` keep it byte-identical.
- A full fixture cycle, from session new through done with a bug, cases and evidence, leaves committed files under `.chough/` only at the paths this requirement lists.

Date and slug names. A new session, evidence entry, bug, inbox entry, journal post and migration receipt SHALL be named `<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>`, the date being the UTC date of its creation and the slug the lowercase ASCII letters and digits of its source (a session key, a case ID or claim, a bug title, a post title), each maximal run of other characters replaced by one hyphen and leading and trailing hyphens trimmed, with the record kind as the slug when nothing is left. The whole name SHALL be at most 80 bytes, the slug cut back at a hyphen when it would exceed that. A record SHALL never be named by a sequence number, a counter or a high-water mark. When a file of that name already exists in the same folder at creation, the new record SHALL get `-` and 6 lowercase hexadecimal digits from 24 fresh random bits (REQ-cli-023's random source), written by create-new; if that name also exists the write SHALL be refused, with nothing written, and SHALL NOT draw again. A record's name SHALL NOT change after creation. The record's front matter SHALL give its name as `id`. Every ID a record had before 0.6.0 (a `BUG-NNNN` or `BUG-<slug>-<hex>` bug, an `OBS-`, `VAL-` or `SNAP-` record, a session key) SHALL be kept in its front matter `aliases` list, and every command and link that takes a record ID SHALL resolve it by `id` or by alias; an alias held by two records SHALL be refused by the command that resolves it and reported by `chough doctor` (REQ-history-012). SpecSync requirement IDs, case IDs, lesson numbering and spec versions SHALL keep their schemes. Trace: DRIVE-27, DRIVE-12, DRIVE-25.

Acceptance Criteria
- `  Fix   LOGIN... now!  ` recorded as a bug on 2026-11-10 is named `2026-11-10-fix-login-now`, and a title with no letter or digit gives `2026-11-10-bug`; an overlong title gives a name of at most 80 bytes that ends without a hyphen.
- Two bugs with the same title on the same day get `2026-11-10-<slug>` and `2026-11-10-<slug>-<6 hex>`; a forced clash of the suffix too is refused with nothing written and no second draw.
- Two branches that each add a bug and an evidence entry on the same day with different titles merge with no conflict.
- A migrated bug with alias `BUG-0012` is shown, updated and linked by `BUG-0012` and by its new name, and a session referencing `OBS-<slug>-<hex>` resolves it to the migrated evidence; an alias given to two records is refused by `bug show` and reported by `chough doctor`.
- No new record's name holds a number taken from a count of existing records.

The session record. An open session's `session.md` front matter SHALL be its checkpoint and SHALL give `kind: session`, `id`, `aliases`, `objective`, `intent_scope`, `modules`, `stage`, `stage_status`, `iteration`, `callers`, `native_change`, `pr`, `criteria`, `requirements`, `cases`, `design`, `files`, `observations`, `bugs`, `blockers`, `waiting_on_human` (each gate with `gate`, `holds` and `opened`, REQ-cli-030), `run_consents` and `next`. Its body SHALL be the story, in these sections in this order: `# <title>` (the objective), `## Goal`, `## Where it stands`, `## Decisions and why`, `## What was verified`, `## Open threads` and `## Timeline` (REQ-history-002). A decision recorded with `chough checkpoint --decision` SHALL be one list item appended to Decisions and why, naming who decided when the decision is a human's (REQ-cli-050) and linking the gate's timeline entry; completed work SHALL be appended to Where it stands; an open question SHALL be one list item in Open threads, resolved by appending its answer to that item's line through `chough checkpoint --resolve-question`; an evidence entry referenced by the session SHALL be one list item in What was verified that links its file. These sections SHALL be the only place the session keeps decisions, completed work and open questions, and `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL read them there (REQ-cli-021), so no field repeats them. Chough SHALL write the Goal from the objective when the session is created and SHALL NOT rewrite the Goal or Where it stands paragraphs afterwards. Trace: DRIVE-24, DRIVE-25, DRIVE-26, FLOW-13.

Acceptance Criteria
- `chough session new` writes a `session.md` whose front matter carries every listed key and whose body has the seven parts in order with the Goal taken from the objective.
- A decision, a completed item, an open question and an evidence reference each appear once, in their section, and `chough next` shows the same decision and question from a fresh process.
- Resolving an open question keeps its line and appends the answer, and `chough next` no longer lists it as open.
- A person's rewrite of the Goal paragraph is kept after a decision and a stage move.

Proof files: logs, key failing lines and external evidence. A raw log SHALL never be committed. The raw output of an executed case SHALL be written to `.chough/local/logs/<evidence id>.log`, and its evidence entry SHALL give the exact command, the SHA-256 of the captured output as its fingerprint and, when a CI run holds the log, `raw_log` naming that run. For a failed or not-run case run, the entry's body SHALL also keep the key failing lines: at most 20 lines and 2,048 bytes of the captured output, with complete terminal escape sequences removed, taken for the `cargo-test` adapter from the first failure block and the `test result:` line, and otherwise from the last non-blank lines of standard error and then standard output; any of them that matches REQ-records-006 SHALL be redacted, never refused, and the entry SHALL say how many were. `chough evidence add --failing-lines <text>` SHALL keep the same for a manual failure, within the same bounds and checked as REQ-records-006 checks other text. `chough evidence add --artifact <path>` and `chough cases record --artifact <path>` SHALL accept an absolute path outside the project: Chough SHALL fingerprint it in place with SHA-256 within a 64 MiB bound and SHALL NOT copy it into the repository; a missing path, a directory, a symlink and a file over 64 MiB SHALL be refused, naming the path on standard error only. It SHALL record the path and fingerprint in `.chough/local/external-artifacts.toml` under a neutral ID `ext-<6 lowercase hex>` from fresh random bits, written by create-new, and the committed entry SHALL give only `external: ext-<hex>` and `fingerprint: sha256:<64 hex>`. On the machine that holds the ID, freshness SHALL re-read the file and report the artifact `current` or `changed`; elsewhere it SHALL be reported `external, not checkable here`, which SHALL be neither a pass nor a staleness of the entry's own content identity. A path outside the project, a local tool path and a raw log SHALL be kept only in `.chough/local/`. Key screenshots are committed under REQ-records-013. Trace: KNOW-35, LIFE-19, FLOW-22, LIFE-26, LIFE-8.

Acceptance Criteria
- `chough cases run` writes its captured output to `.chough/local/logs/`, and the committed entry carries the exact command and the output's SHA-256; no file Git tracks under `.chough/` holds a raw log.
- A failing `cargo-test` case's entry keeps its panic lines and its `test result:` line, at most 20 lines and 2,048 bytes, with no escape sequence; a failing line holding a home path is stored as `<redacted:home-path>` and the entry counts it.
- An absolute artifact outside the project is fingerprinted in place, its path appears only in `.chough/local/external-artifacts.toml`, and the committed entry holds only the neutral ID and the fingerprint.
- A missing path, a directory, a symlink and a 64 MiB plus one byte file are refused with nothing recorded.
- Changing the external file makes the artifact read `changed` on that machine; with `.chough/local/` removed the entry reads `external, not checkable here` and is neither reported passed nor stale because of that artifact.

No leaks in committed records. Before writing any committed record, Chough SHALL check every value it writes, in front matter and body, including recorded commands, summaries, reasons, decisions, relayed words and places, notes, limitations, titles and actor values, for: an absolute path under a home, temporary or system root (`/Users/`, `/home/`, `/root/`, `/private/`, `/tmp/`, `/var/`, `/Volumes/`, `/mnt/`) or a Windows drive path; a `~/` path; the local host name, and the local user name when it appears inside a path or as `<user>@<host>`; an email address; and credentials: GitHub, GitLab, Slack, AWS and model-provider token forms, private key blocks, bearer and basic authorization values, JSON web tokens, and `password`, `secret`, `token` or `api_key` assignments with a value of 8 or more characters. A value that matches SHALL refuse the write as `refused:leak`, naming the field and the kind of match and never the matched text, with every file byte-identical. With `--redact`, each match SHALL instead be replaced by `<redacted:<kind>>` and the write SHALL proceed, saying how many values were redacted. A human's configured display name (REQ-records-008) SHALL NOT count as a user name. `chough doctor` SHALL scan every file Git tracks under `.chough/` and `knowledge/` for the same patterns and SHALL report each as a `leak` finding with the file, the line and the kind, never the text; the verify and CI lanes SHALL run that scan and fail on a finding. Trace: LIFE-26, LIFE-17, FLOW-22.

Acceptance Criteria
- Each pattern kind, placed in an evidence summary, a decision, a relayed `--words`, a bug note and a recorded command, refuses the write with `refused:leak` naming the field and kind, the output never contains the matched text, and every file is unchanged.
- The same writes with `--redact` store `<redacted:<kind>>` and report the count.
- A decision naming the configured human display name is written; the same name inside `/Users/<name>/` is refused.
- With one committed record holding a home path, `chough doctor` reports a `leak` finding with its file, line and kind, without the path, and exits 1; `fledge lanes run verify` fails on it.
- The records of a full fixture cycle run inside a temporary directory hold no absolute path, user name or host name.

The acting agent. Each timeline entry (REQ-history-002), evidence entry and bug SHALL record the acting agent when it is known, as `actor` with `agent`, `model` and `terminal`, each only when known: `CHOUGH_ACTOR`, `CHOUGH_ACTOR_MODEL` and `CHOUGH_HC_TERMINAL` SHALL set them; otherwise the agent SHALL be `claude-code` when `CLAUDECODE` is set and the terminal SHALL be `HC_TERMINAL_ID` when it is set. The terminal SHALL be the hc terminal address or name, such as `t370`, and never a file path, a host name or a network address. A value that fails the check of REQ-records-006 SHALL be left out with a warning on standard error, and an unknown actor SHALL leave the field out; neither SHALL fail a command. `chough next` and `chough status` SHALL show the last actor, and `chough status` SHALL show each listed evidence entry's actor. The actor is an unauthenticated claim and SHALL never stand in for a human decision (FLOW-16). Trace: LIFE-17, LIFE-26, FLOW-16.

Acceptance Criteria
- With the three override variables set, a stage move, an evidence add and a bug add each record that agent, model and terminal; with only `CLAUDECODE` and `HC_TERMINAL_ID` set they record `claude-code` and that terminal.
- With none set, no record has `actor`, `chough next` shows no last actor, and every command succeeds.
- A terminal value holding a home path is left out with a warning and the command succeeds.
- The shared test fixture clears the five variables, so the suite gives the same records under Claude Code and hc.

A human's gate approval drives the native approval as that human. Chough SHALL read human identities from configuration, never from its source: the user configuration file `chough/identity.toml` under `XDG_CONFIG_HOME` (by default `~/.config`), overridden by `.chough/local/identity.toml` when present, each `[[human]]` giving `name`, the display name records show, optional `aliases`, and `specsync_actor`, the actor SpecSync records. When a gate that drives a native step (REQ-cli-030) is closed with a human's decision (REQ-cli-050, REQ-cli-059, REQ-cli-061), Chough SHALL resolve `--decided-by` to one configured human by name or alias and SHALL run, before it records anything, `specsync change approve <id> --actor <specsync_actor> --note <note>` for a gate that drives approval, the note giving the human's exact words, where and when they decided, and the agent that relayed or recorded it, or `specsync change review <id> --reviewer <specsync_actor> --verdict <pass or block>` for one that drives review, with the verdict given as `--verdict` on the close, which SHALL be required there and SHALL never be read from the words. A human decision that is neither an approval nor a review, such as a request for changes, SHALL be recorded with `--no-native`, which closes the gate with the relay and runs nothing; Chough SHALL NOT decide which case applies from the words. When SpecSync refuses, Chough SHALL pass its output and exit code through and record nothing; when it succeeds, Chough SHALL close the gate with the relay and add the decision, which SHALL name the native step run. `--decided-by` naming no configured human, or two, SHALL be refused as `refused:human-identity-unknown`, naming both configuration files and the keys to add, before anything runs; Chough SHALL NOT guess an identity or fall back to an agent account. A gate that drives no native step SHALL record no human. An agent that approves or reviews on authority the human gave in advance, without the human answering that gate, SHALL record the native step as the acting agent, `<agent>-<terminal>` (REQ-cli-029), quoting the human's earlier words and where they said them, so only a decision made at that gate is in the human's name (FLOW-24). No source file, skill, template or document SHALL name a specific person as the default human. The relay remains an unauthenticated claim (FLOW-16). Trace: FLOW-23, FLOW-24, FLOW-16, FLOW-10, LIFE-26.

Acceptance Criteria
- With a configured human and a scope gate that drives approval, closing it with that human's relay runs `specsync change approve` once with the configured actor and a note holding the words, place and relaying agent, then closes the gate and records the decision.
- The same at an acceptance gate with `--verdict pass` runs `specsync change review --reviewer` as that human with that verdict, and without `--verdict` it refuses before anything runs; `--no-native` closes a driving gate with the relay and starts no SpecSync process.
- A SpecSync refusal's output and exit code pass through, the gate stays open and nothing is written.
- An unconfigured or ambiguous `--decided-by` refuses with `refused:human-identity-unknown` naming both files, and no SpecSync process starts.
- `.chough/local/identity.toml` overrides the user file; a gate that drives nothing closes with no native call.
- An approval or review on authority given in advance names the agent account `<agent>-<terminal>` as the SpecSync actor and quotes the human's earlier words and place, and never the human as the actor.
- A search of `src/`, `skills/`, `docs/` and `README.md` finds no person's name or account given as a default identity.

Migration from 0.5.x. `chough migrate` SHALL read a project's 0.5.x records, write nothing, and print the plan: each 0.5.x file with its SHA-256 and what it becomes, each 0.6.0 file it would write, every value it would redact by kind (REQ-records-006), and every file it would remove without carrying it, with why, and SHALL end with the plan's SHA-256. `chough migrate --apply <plan digest>` SHALL refuse, writing nothing, unless the plan it builds has that digest, so nothing is migrated that was not previewed first; it SHALL also refuse, writing nothing, while any native change in the project is not archived, naming each, so it never runs while a change is open, and unless the human's consent is given, either as `--consent <source>` naming who consented, their words and where, which the receipt records as a relayed claim, or as a standing `migration` preference with its source (REQ-cli-013), and Chough SHALL NOT infer consent from the digest or from any other record; it SHALL also refuse, writing nothing, while a 0.5.x file to be removed differs from its bytes at HEAD or is untracked, naming each, so Git holds every byte it removes. It SHALL then write the 0.6.0 tree by create-new only and SHALL refuse, writing nothing more, when a file it would write already exists with other bytes; it SHALL read each written file back and compare its digest; it SHALL write the receipt `.chough/archive/migrations/<YYYY-MM-DD>-from-0-5.md` listing, for every file before and after, its path, size and SHA-256, the redactions by file, field and kind, every removed file with why and the commit that holds it, and the old-to-new ID map; and only then SHALL it remove the 0.5.x files, each only when its bytes still match the plan. It SHALL never weaken a SpecSync archive: before removing anything it SHALL read the native validity of every archived change whose acceptance manifest lists a file it would remove, at most 8 reads at once, read them again after the removal, and, if any archive that read valid no longer does, restore every removed file byte for byte and refuse, naming those archives. A file written by an interrupted apply with the planned bytes SHALL count as done on the next apply, and a second apply on a migrated tree SHALL report nothing to do. The mapping SHALL be: each open session, legacy `.chough/session.json` included, becomes a session folder whose timeline holds, in order, every transition of its selected history lineage, the legacy log's entries going to the session that adopted them; each archived session, and each session rolled into `knowledge/attachments/`, becomes an archived story; each observation an open session references becomes an evidence entry of that session, each one an archived session or a bug references becomes a receipt of that story or bug, and others are removed; a PNG or JPEG artifact of a carried observation that fits the bounds of REQ-records-013 is kept beside its session or story, and other artifacts are removed; each bug becomes a Markdown bug; inbox entries move to their session's `agent/inbox/`; every 0.5.x ID is kept as an alias (REQ-records-003), and an ID whose record was removed without being carried SHALL resolve as `removed`, naming the receipt, never as current or passed; and `.chough/transitions.jsonl`, `.chough/history/`, `.chough/pruned.jsonl`, `.chough/session.v1.json`, `.chough/artifacts/` other than files an open bug names, shelved 0.5.x sessions and the generated or copied vault content of REQ-cli-044 are removed after they are listed. Every file migration writes SHALL pass REQ-records-006 with redaction, so no home-folder path, user name or credential survives in a rewritten record; a file it keeps byte for byte (an open bug's fixture, a `library/` snapshot or brief) that matches SHALL be listed in the plan and the receipt as a `leak` finding for a person to fix, never changed silently and never kept unreported. The receipt SHALL say that Git history still holds what earlier commits leaked, which this migration does not rewrite. Case definitions and preferences SHALL stay byte-identical. Removal SHALL follow REQ-records-012. Trace: DRIVE-27, LIFE-20, LIFE-21, LIFE-8, KNOW-10, KNOW-11, KNOW-30, KNOW-31, KNOW-34, LIFE-26.

Acceptance Criteria
- Fixtures captured from a project at every released 0.x version, 0.1.0 to 0.5.0, each built from its release tag, migrate to the same kind of 0.6.0 tree with every record readable (#213).
- `--apply` without a digest, or with the digest of an earlier plan, refuses and writes nothing; `--apply` with the preview's digest proceeds.
- With a native change that is not archived, or with neither `--consent` nor a standing `migration` preference, `--apply` with the preview's digest refuses and writes nothing, naming the open change or the missing consent; with consent the receipt records its source.
- With a SpecSync stub whose archive reads invalid once a listed file is gone, `--apply` restores every removed file byte for byte and refuses naming that archive.
- A rewritten record that held a home-folder path holds `<redacted:home-path>` and the receipt counts it; a kept fixture holding one is listed as a `leak` finding and left unchanged; the receipt says Git history is not rewritten.
- On a 0.5.x fixture with a legacy checkpoint, adopted history, two open and seven archived sessions, rolled sessions in the vault, a bug of each ID form, inbox entries and old proof, `chough migrate` writes nothing and lists every file, target, redaction and removal.
- `--apply` with an uncommitted or untracked 0.5.x file refuses naming it, with nothing written.
- `--apply` writes every planned file and the receipt, removes the 0.5.x files, and afterwards every record, alias and timeline entry is readable by `next`, `status`, `bug show`, `session list` and `timing`; the receipt's before and after digests match the files at the earlier and the new commit.
- With a target that already exists with other bytes, `--apply` refuses and writes nothing more; after an apply interrupted between writes, the next apply completes and the result equals an uninterrupted one; a second apply on the result reports nothing to do.
- Case definition files and `.chough/preferences.json` are byte-identical before and after.
- Every transition of the selected lineage appears once, in order, in its session's timeline, and every archived session, the rolled ones included, is an archived story.
- A bug linking an observation that was removed without being carried shows it as `removed` with the receipt named, and `chough next` never counts it as current or passed.
- Regression for the local bug where history writes refused once the adopting session rolled into the vault: a 0.5.x fixture whose adopting session sits in `knowledge/attachments/`, with `.chough/transitions.jsonl` unchanged, migrates; the legacy entries land in that session's archived story, and afterwards `checkpoint --awaiting-human`, `--close-gate` and a stage move all succeed. The same writes are first recorded refusing on the last build before #142 (90e5de6f^), with the same tree recorded as observed on 0.5.0.

Journal and feed. The knowledge vault's journal SHALL be dated Markdown posts in `knowledge/journal/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md`, each with front matter giving `id`, `title`, `type: journal`, `tags`, `date`, `kind` (`shipped`, `closed`, `intent`, `spec`, `broke` or `learned`), `links` and, for a finished session, `record`, the path of its archived story. When a session archives itself at its move into done (REQ-history-006), Chough SHALL write a `shipped` post, or a `closed` post for a session closed without done, by create-new: the title is the session's objective, the body is the story's first Outcome or Where it stands paragraph cut to at most 1,200 bytes at a sentence end, followed by a line linking the PR when the session names one, the archived story and, when the session's native change is archived, its `.specsync/archive/changes/` folder, so the post is short and the story holds the full record. The journal and its feed SHALL be the timeline of archived changes: `knowledge/index.md` SHALL present them as that timeline and SHALL link `.specsync/archive/changes/` for changes archived before the journal began (REQ-cli-043), and no other timeline page SHALL be generated. `chough journal add --kind <kind> --title <title> --body <text> [--link <link>]...` SHALL write any other post by create-new, refusing a body over 1,200 bytes. Chough SHALL never rewrite or remove a post, so a person's edit is kept. `knowledge/journal/feed.xml` SHALL be an Atom feed of the newest 20 posts by date and then name, generated from the posts with identical bytes for the same posts, and `chough library index` SHALL regenerate it, with `--check` covering it (REQ-cli-047). The journal SHALL copy no record: it links them. Trace: KNOW-33, KNOW-30, KNOW-31, KNOW-15, KNOW-4, KNOW-14.

Acceptance Criteria
- The move into done of a session with a PR and an archived native change writes one `shipped` post whose body is at most 1,200 bytes and links the PR, `.chough/archive/sessions/<id>.md` and the change's archive folder, and `feed.xml` lists it.
- `knowledge/index.md` names the journal and feed as the timeline of archived changes and links `.specsync/archive/changes/`, and no `timeline.md` or `timeline/` is generated.
- A person's edit to a post survives a later move into done and `library index`, and a post name that already exists is never overwritten.
- `chough journal add` writes a post of each kind, and a body over 1,200 bytes is refused with nothing written.
- Regenerating `feed.xml` twice gives identical bytes, it parses as XML, and `library index --check` fails naming it after a hand edit.

Removal only of committed bytes. No Chough command SHALL remove a committed record or working file, or move it out of its folder, which covers a session's `session.md`, its `evidence/` entries, screenshots and `agent/` files, a 0.5.x file during migration, a shelved session and an archived story, unless that file's exact bytes are committed at the current commit (HEAD). Rewriting a record in place under REQ-records-001 is not a removal. A file Chough would remove whose bytes differ from HEAD, or that HEAD does not hold, SHALL be kept in place and reported with its path and the reason, and the command SHALL say how to finish once the file is committed. A command that keeps a file this way SHALL NOT report that file removed. No Chough command SHALL remove or rewrite an archived story's existing bytes, and nothing SHALL trim `.chough/archive/sessions/` by count or age: every finished session stays as one story file, with its screenshot folder when it has one, so links to it never break; a correction only appends (REQ-history-015). Trace: LIFE-20, KNOW-34, LIFE-8, DRIVE-24, DRIVE-25, KNOW-30.

Acceptance Criteria
- A session finished with an uncommitted `agent/` file keeps that file and its folder and reports it; after the file is committed, `chough doctor --fix` removes the folder, and the file's bytes are in Git at the commit that removed it.
- `chough migrate --apply` refuses to remove a 0.5.x file changed since HEAD and removes it once the change is committed.
- No test fixture cycle, migration or doctor fix leaves a file removed whose bytes HEAD did not hold before the removal.
- With 40 archived stories of every age, a move into done, `session new`, `doctor --fix` and `library index` leave all 40 byte-identical in place.

Key screenshots beside the story. `chough evidence add --screenshot <path>` SHALL commit one small key screenshot with its evidence entry: a PNG or JPEG file of at most 524,288 bytes, at most 5 per session and at most 2,097,152 bytes per session in all. Chough SHALL remove PNG `tEXt`, `zTXt`, `iTXt`, `tIME` and `eXIf` chunks and JPEG `APP1` to `APP15` and `COM` segments before writing, so the committed image carries no metadata, SHALL write it by create-new as `.chough/sessions/<session>/evidence/<evidence id>.png` (or `.jpg`) beside its entry, and the entry SHALL give `screenshot` as that file name and `fingerprint` as the SHA-256 of the committed bytes. Another format, a file over a bound, a symlink, and a sixth screenshot or one past the session total SHALL be refused with nothing written, naming the bound and saying to crop or compress it, or to record it by fingerprint with `--artifact` (REQ-records-005). When the session finishes, each screenshot SHALL move to `.chough/archive/sessions/<session>/<evidence id>.<ext>`, a folder beside the story file that exists only when the session has a screenshot, and the story's What was verified line for that entry SHALL link it; the move SHALL follow REQ-records-012. Chough cannot see what an image shows, so the skill SHALL tell the agent to check a screenshot for personal information before adding it. These bounds and this layout are the plan's proposal for Leif to confirm at scope approval. Trace: KNOW-35, KNOW-34, LIFE-26, DRIVE-24.

Acceptance Criteria
- A 500 KiB PNG with a `tEXt` and an `eXIf` chunk is committed beside its entry without those chunks, and the entry's fingerprint is the SHA-256 of the committed file.
- A 513 KiB file, a GIF, a symlink, a sixth screenshot and one that takes the session past 2 MiB are each refused with nothing written, naming the bound and the remedies.
- At finish, the screenshot is at `.chough/archive/sessions/<session>/<evidence id>.png` with identical bytes, the story links it, and a session with no screenshot has no folder beside its story.

Chough's records stay out of SpecSync's verification. The folders Chough writes while work is in progress, `.chough/sessions/`, `.chough/archive/` and `.chough/bugs/`, SHALL hold only Chough's records: no case definition, preference, reading guide or other input that a change's verification needs SHALL be written under them, and `.chough/cases/`, `.chough/preferences.json`, `.chough/README.md` and `knowledge/` SHALL stay outside them. These three prefixes are what a project lists in SpecSync's documented exclusion, `verification_ignored_paths` in `.specsync/sdd.json` (SpecSync 6.1.2 and later), so that a Chough record written after `specsync change check --commit`, whether left untracked or committed, leaves the recorded verification current, in the author's tree and in a reviewer's clean checkout alike; `.chough/local/` is already Git-ignored and never part of it. Chough SHALL read that policy and SHALL never write it: `chough doctor` SHALL report `records_in_verification` (REQ-history-012) while `.specsync/sdd.json` exists and its list lacks any of the three prefixes, naming the missing entries, the SpecSync version that supports them and that adding them is an ordinary reviewed change to `.specsync/sdd.json`; `chough init` SHALL print the same advice; and the migration plan and receipt SHALL list it as a follow-up (REQ-records-009). `chough next` SHALL say when Chough writes are safe: with the three entries in force, that Chough's records may be written and committed at any point of the native order; without them, that Chough's records are committed before `change check --commit` and nothing under `.chough/` is written until finalize. When SpecSync refuses the list because an open change's affected paths overlap it, Chough SHALL pass that refusal through and name the change. Trace: DRIVE-4, FLOW-16.

Acceptance Criteria
- With the three entries listed and real SpecSync at the CI pin, an untracked evidence entry present while `change check --commit` runs leaves verification current in that tree and in a clean clone of the pushed commit, whose workspace digest matches the recorded one (spec-sync #1045's case); the same steps without the entries leave the clone's verification stale, as the control.
- With the three entries listed, a `chough checkpoint`, a `chough evidence add` and a `chough bug add` written after `change check --commit`, and then committed, leave `specsync change status` reporting verification current and the audit passing, and the review then records (the #212 case); without the entries the same writes make verification stale, as the control.
- A case definition changed under `.chough/cases/` after `change check --commit` still makes verification stale, so nothing a change's verification needs is hidden.
- With a prefix missing, `chough doctor` reports `records_in_verification` naming the missing entries and writes nothing; with all three listed it reports nothing; `.specsync/sdd.json` is byte-identical after every Chough command.
- `chough next` says Chough's writes are safe at any point with the entries in force, and gives the commit-first order without them.
